facts.statement: Between 30 and 40 fossil specimens of Darwinopterus were found in the Tiaojishan Formation, dating to the Middle Jurassic period approximately 160.89 to 160.25 million years ago.
facts.quote: Between 30 and 40 fossil specimens have been identified, all collected from the Tiaojishan Formation, which dates to the middle Jurassic period, 160.89–160.25 Ma ago.

facts.statement: The type species, Darwinopterus modularis, was first described in February 2010.
facts.quote: The type species, D. modularis, was described in February 2010.

facts.statement: In all species of Darwinopterus, the teeth were widely spaced, spike-like, and set in sockets with raised margins, with the longest teeth located at the jaw tips.
facts.quote: The teeth in all species were spaced widely with the longest teeth at the jaw tips. The teeth were spike-like in form, and set into tooth sockets with raised margins.

facts.statement: Unlike other wukongopterids, the male head crest of Darwinopterus was supported by a thin bony skull extension with a serrated edge, likely to anchor a larger keratinous crest.
facts.quote: Unlike other wukongopterids, the head crest found in males was supported by a thin bony extension of the skull, with a serrated top edge. The serrations probably helped anchor an even larger keratin extension.

facts.statement: Specimens of Darwinopterus are divided into four distinct species, primarily distinguished by the size and shape of their teeth.
facts.quote: Specimens of Darwinopterus have been divided into four distinct species, based largely on the size and shape of their teeth.

facts.statement: In D. camposi, the fourth phalange of the wing finger is shorter than the first, a unique trait among all species of Darwinopterus.
facts.quote: The fourth phalange of the wing finger (the outermost bone) is shorter than the first (the innermost finger bone), unique among species of Darwinopterus.

facts.statement: In 2024, it was suggested that the genus Darwinopterus is polyphyletic, with phylogenetic analyses placing the other three species in various positions rather than as a single group.
facts.quote: In 2024, it has been suggested that the genus Darwinopterus is polyphyletic based on phylogenetic analyses by Hone et al. (2024), who recovered the other three species in various positions.

facts.statement: Numerous well-preserved specimens, including an egg, have allowed researchers to deduce Darwinopterus biology, such as growth patterns, life history, reproduction, and potential sexual variation.
facts.quote: Because Darwinopterus is known from numerous well-preserved specimens including an egg, researchers have been able to deduce various aspects of its biology, including growth patterns and life history, reproduction, and possible variation between sexes.

facts.statement: The hypothesis of sexual dimorphism in Darwinopterus has been criticized; researcher Kevin Padian suggested that crest size and shape may change with age, similar to ceratopsian dinosaurs, rather than indicating sex.
facts.quote: However, this hypothesis has been criticized. Pterosaur researcher Kevin Padian questioned some of the conclusions drawn by Lü et al., suggesting in a 2011 interview that, in other animals with elaborate display crests (such as ceratopsian dinosaurs), the size and shape of the crests change dramatically with age.

facts.statement: In 2015, the "Mrs T" specimen was reassigned to the genus Kunpengopterus, and in 2021 it was classified as the species Kunpengopterus antipollicatus.
facts.quote: In 2015, Wang e.a. reassigned the "Mrs T" specimen to Kunpengopterus, and in 2021 it was classified as a specimen of the new species Kunpengopterus antipollicatus.

facts.statement: Darwinopterus eggs had a parchment-like, soft shell, similar to those of later pterosaurs and modern reptiles.
facts.quote: Like the eggs of later pterosaurs and modern reptiles, the eggs of Darwinopterus had a parchment-like, soft shell.

facts.statement: Darwinopterus eggs weighed about 6 grams when laid but could double in weight due to moisture absorption by the time of hatching.
facts.quote: The eggs of Darwinopterus would have weighed about 6 g when they were laid, but due to moisture intake, they may have doubled in weight by the time of hatching.

facts.statement: David Unwin suggested that Darwinopterus likely laid many small eggs that were buried, and that juveniles could fly immediately upon hatching with little to no parental care.
facts.quote: David Unwin, a co-author of the paper, suggested that Darwinopterus probably laid many small eggs at a time and buried them, and that juveniles could fly upon hatching, requiring little to no parental care.

facts.statement: A 2015 report of the specimen's counterplate revealed a second egg in the body, indicating that Darwinopterus had two active ovaries, each producing one egg at a time.
facts.quote: However, in 2015, the counterplate of the specimen was reported, IVPP V18403, which showed a single additional egg present in the body, indicating that there were two active ovaries, each of which producing a single egg at a time.

facts.statement: Darwinopterus was likely a saltatorial insectivore that hopped through trees and on the ground, similar to modern songbirds.
facts.quote: Instead, it appears to have been a saltatorial insectivore, hopping around both in the trees and on the ground, akin to some modern songbirds.

facts.statement: Researchers suggest the robust teeth of D. robustodens were adapted for feeding on hard-shelled beetles.
facts.quote: The robust teeth of D. robustodens, for example, may have been used to feed on hard-shelled beetles.

facts.statement: Darwinopterus is an extinct genus of pterosaur discovered in China and named in honor of Charles Darwin.
facts.quote: Darwinopterus es un género extinto de pterosaurio, descubierto en China y nombrado en honor a Charles Darwin.

facts.statement: The genus is known from between 30 and 40 fossil specimens all collected from the Middle Jurassic Tiaojishan Formation.
facts.quote: Se le conoce por entre 30 y 40 especímenes fósiles, todos recogidos en la formación Tiaojishan, que data del Jurásico medio.

facts.statement: The type species exhibits traits of both long-tailed (Rhamphorhynchoidea) and short-tailed (Pterodactyloidea) pterosaurs and is described as a transitional fossil between these two groups.
facts.quote: La especie tipo presenta rasgos de ambos tipos principales de pterosaurios, los de cola larga (Rhamphorhynchoidea) y los de cola corta (Pterodactyloidea), y se ha descrito como un fósil de transición entre ambos grupos.

facts.statement: The genus exhibited sexual dimorphism, with females lacking a crest and having wider hips than males.
facts.quote: Este género presentaba dimorfismo sexual. Las hembras carecen de cresta y sus caderas son más anchas que las de los machos

facts.statement: The four species are distinguished mainly by crest shape and tooth type, suggesting each specialized in a different diet.
facts.quote: Las cuatro especies se distinguen principalmente por la forma de la cresta y el tipo de dientes, pues parece que cada una de ellas se especializó en una dieta diferente.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen ZMNH M8782 is fairly well-preserved but lacks important parts of some limbs.
